text:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - capacity-tier routing anomaly. High rate of hosted traffic being routed to Dedicated pools (us-west-2). Affected tenants: tenant_azura, tenant-clix. Detect: sudden dedicated pool saturation + increased billing signal. runbook: /playbooks/routing/fallback.md 
Opal (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Jumping to the routing logs now. @Jamal you free to pair? :wave:
Jamal (eng-sre): here, pulling decision logs. Saw a burst ~ 1832104200 where policy evaluation started sending hosted requests to dedicated variants. grabbing sample log: 
```
[1832104212] req_id=abc123 tenant=tenant_azura route_eval: matched policy="tier-fallback-hosted" -> target=dedicated_pool_uswest2 reason="spillover_enabled"
[1832104212] req_id=abc123 model_variant=redwood-3b-quant target_pool=dedicated_pool_uswest2
```
Rita (serving): that policy name looks like the 'spillover' rule. last deploy touched routing precedence yesterday at 09:15 UTC by eng-deploy-bot. Could be precedence inversion.
Opal (oncall): timeline: alert at 1832104560, logs show matches starting ~1832104200, dedicated cpu/gpu saturation alarms at 1832104300.
Jamal (eng-sre): I pulled the policy YAML from prod config-store, looks wrong — hosted fallback has higher precedence number (meaning higher priority) than dedicated-override. snippet: 
```
policies:
  - id: dedicated-override
    precedence: 50
    match:
      tier: dedicated
    action: route: dedicated_pool
  - id: hosted-spillover
    precedence: 100
    match:
      tier: hosted
    action: route: dedicated_pool
```
In our evaluator lower precedence value should win. So hosted-spillover with 100 ended up overriding dedicated because we accidentally flipped comparator in last deploy.
eng-deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-11-02T09:15 by ci-user (revision: ab9f). Config change: routing/eval: comparator switched from '<' to '>' in comparator module.
Rita (serving): confirmed. comparator inversion means "higher number wins" now, so hosted spillover (100) outranks dedicated override (50) -> hosted -> dedicated. Bad.
Opal (oncall): immediate mitigation options? We can temporarily disable hosted-spillover policy or flip precedence back. Which is faster?
Jamal (eng-sre): quickest is disable hosted-spillover via admin API (no restart). I'll post the command.
Jamal (eng-sre): `curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/policies/hosted-spillover/disable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"` -> returns 202. Doing now.
[~30s later]
eng-deploy-bot: API response: 202 Accepted -> hosted-spillover disabled by Jamal.
Opal (oncall): metrics: dedicated pool saturation dropping, queued requests draining. latency normalizing for affected tenants. Good.
Lena (support): are any paying customers impacted? We had 3 SLO violations for tenant_azura in the last 15m. I'll open a support thread and prepare an incident notice.
Marco (product): hold on messaging until we have a clear customer impact summary. We should avoid implying data loss. Focus on routing misassignment + mitigation.
Jamal (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: recent routing evaluator comparator change reversed precedence semantics. This allowed spillover rules (intended to be lower priority) to override dedicated isolation.
Rita (serving): immediate next steps: 1) revert comparator change in config repo, 2) add unit test to ensure precedence comparator semantics, 3) run a quick canary in staging for policy evaluation, 4) verify that admin disable is safe - it is for now.
Opal (oncall): I've taken IC role for initial triage. Jamal you're tech lead. Rita you're on rollback plan. Marco, please coordinate customer comms with Lena.
Lena (support): drafting message: "We detected short-lived routing misassignment causing elevated latency for a small number of customers between 09:10-09:25 UTC. The issue is mitigated; we're completing a postmortem." Will share draft in #support-drafts.
Jamal (eng-sre): rolling back comparator patch now. 
eng-deploy-bot: revert PR merged (rev: ab9f -> ab9f-rollback). Triggering config rollout to routing-eval pool.
Opal (oncall): watch logs for reappearance. Rita, can you validate a sample tenant pinned to dedicated does not get routed to hosted/dedicated incorrectly after revert?
Rita (serving): running validation script: `python tools/check_routing.py --tenant tenant_azura --trace 100` -> sample outputs show correct match: `policy=dedicated-override -> target=dedicated_pool_uswest2` on all traces.
Jamal (eng-sre): metrics check: no new dedicated saturation alerts for 10m, error rate back within baseline for affected tenants. cost delta looked scary for 16 minutes but now normal.
Marco (product): good. Can we add a guard in the deployment pipeline to reject comparator semantics changes without explicit approval? Also add an integration test that deploys a contrived precedence set.
Opal (oncall): agreed. I'll file follow-ups: (1) root cause postmortem, (2) deploy gate for comparator code, (3) add policy evaluation unit + staging integration test, (4) customer outreach review.
Lena (support): posted customer notice draft in #support-drafts & pinged Marco.
Jamal (eng-sre): estimated blast radius: 4 dedicated pools temporarily saturated, 6 tenants saw >SLO latency, no data corruption, no auth incidents.
Rita (serving): long-term: add a liveness check that flags when priority/precedence ordering deviates from saved source-of-truth; tie to alerting so we detect comparator flips early.
Opal (oncall): handing off to Jamal for postmortem and follow-ups. I'll go to sleep after a brief watch. Please call if it resurfaces.
Jamal (eng-sre): taking IC for follow-up, will schedule RCA and include timeline + patch. Raising severity to SEV1 -> SEV2-> mitigated; final classification after RCA.
eng-deploy-bot: deploy logs: routing-eval reverted and rollout completed at 1832105320.
Opal (oncall): closing incident channel for live mitigation. Follow-up tickets: DOCS-142 (runbook update), SRE-293 (deploy gate), SERVE-88 (policy unit tests).
Lena (support): will send customer notification at T+2h after internal review.
Marco (product): thanks team. Good containment. We'll aim for postmortem by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
